solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Someone preferring not to move is bored travelling with him

indicators.note: letters that are travelling are on the move, so they do not stay in their printed order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stay-at-home type grows restless and fed up whenever they have to go on a journey with a male companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A homebird is an informal British word for a person who likes staying at home rather than going out or relocating.

clue.text: Love rice wine, mostly followed by a Japanese port

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the drink's name is dropped

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
sake is Japanese rice wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's affection for sake leads them on to a Japanese harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major city and seaport on Honshu, the main island of Japan.

clue.text: River — it may mark the spot between two points

indicators.note: a thing placed between two others sits inside them, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: E for east, a compass point, taken twice
X marks the spot on a treasure map

explanation.surface: A cartographer notes where a stream crosses the map, marking its place between two locations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England, flowing to the sea at Exmouth.

clue.text: Murdoch, for one, hailed primarily from Dublin?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the word before it counts

blocks.note: Iris Murdoch was a celebrated novelist
the opening letter of hailed

explanation.surface: A question about where the novelist Iris Murdoch came from: she was in fact born in Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: being from Dublin is one way of being Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Ireland's capital city is Irish by nationality, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: A secret surfing location?

blocks.note: surface reading: a hidden beach where only insiders go to catch waves
setter's reading: surfing the internet, at a hidden part of it reached only with special software

explanation.walkthrough: Surfing suggests waves and boards, but here it means browsing online.
explanation.definitionFit: This concealed portion of the internet needs special browsers to reach and is used for anonymous, often illicit, browsing.

clue.text: Provide financial investment here again

blocks.note: first meaning: to fund or sponsor a venture
second meaning: returned, as in 'I'm ___'

explanation.surface: An investor returns to put money into a project for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To support with money is one sense of the verb; someone who has returned is said to be home again in the other.

clue.text: Last drink? Down the hatch!

blocks.note: the one at the bottom of a list comes last
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone calls for the final round at the bar and cheers as it is downed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal toasts urging people to drain their glasses in one go.

clue.text: Profile clubs playing in various cities?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a show that is playing is on
a tour takes a team or band to many cities

explanation.surface: A sports writer profiles football clubs who play matches around many different cities.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or silhouette of a shape, such as a face or a hill, is its outer shape, the line traced around its edge.

clue.text: Run fantastic 400m, perhaps

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An athlete runs a brilliant time over one lap of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The 400 metres is one example of a track event, so 'perhaps' signals an example of a contest of speed.

clue.text: It’s annoying, and I ultimately bluster and yell when holding it

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the following word is used
something holding another keeps it inside, so the short word goes within the longer one

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of bluster
to rant is to shout angrily
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who blusters and shouts while making a point is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'and' is a link; the I that follows it is the opening letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is a thing that causes irritation, so the phrase describes exactly what such a thing does.

clue.text: Programme on which to see celebs walk out with host

definitions.text: Programme on which to see celebs

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Famous guests stroll onto a television set alongside the presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk out' reads as a phrasal verb, but out is the anagram signal for walk and host together.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity guests appear on chat programmes where a presenter interviews them on television.

clue.text: British actress regularly in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word must be judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: something done every night happens regularly

explanation.surface: A British actress turns up at auditions again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Keira Knightley is a British film star; 'in audition' looks like part of the acting story but signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Keira Knightley, star of Pride and Prejudice and Pirates of the Caribbean, is an English film performer.

clue.text: Old blokes periodically forming part of an orchestra

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
the first, third and fifth letters of blokes

explanation.surface: Elderly men turn up now and then to join an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: This double-reed woodwind instrument is a member of every symphony orchestra's woodwind section.

clue.text: Ancient area of Casablanca, say, seemed inaccessible to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: spans the end of seemed and the start of inaccessible

explanation.surface: A tourist finds the old quarter of a Moroccan city somewhat hard to get into.
explanation.definitionFit: A medina is the walled old quarter of a North African city, Casablanca being one example.

clue.text: Fast Australian runner behind rival

blocks.note: the emu is a speedy flightless Australian bird
running behind schedule means being late

explanation.surface: A quick Australian sprinter trails behind a competitor in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a bird; 'rival' is a verb here, not the competitor it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to match or equal their achievements, which is the verb sense of rival.

clue.text: In the most serious case, a couple starts to regret selling before time

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
a couple is two
the first letters of regret and selling
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: At the extreme, a pair of people come to rue selling a property too early.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means if the worst happens, describing the most pessimistic possible outcome of a situation.

clue.text: Bar in Munich is taken on by family member

indicators.note: something taken on is absorbed inside the other party, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: bro is short for brother
ist is German for is, and Munich is in Germany

explanation.surface: A sibling takes over the running of a pub in a Bavarian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant or bar serving simple food and wine.

clue.text: Great quantity left out of garden material

indicators.note: something left out of a thing is removed from it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
mulch is a covering spread over soil in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener has a big heap of compost left unused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a verb meaning remaining, but it is the abbreviation removed from the garden material.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot of something, a large amount, is the noun sense of this common word.

clue.text: Cover with vocals over a backing beat

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
rapping is rhythmic speaking over a backing track

explanation.surface: A musician records a cover version, singing over a backing rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song, but it is the noun meaning a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper or material put around a present or parcel serves as its outer covering.

clue.text: Big fuss surrounding limits of diet supplement

indicators.note: something surrounding another goes around it, so one piece is placed inside the other
the limits of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are used

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
the first and last letters of diet

explanation.surface: People make a great commotion about the edges of a diet plan and taking vitamins.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplement something is to make an addition that increases it, as the phrasal verb means.

clue.text: Mini cheese sandwiches for a particular market

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective use of the answer

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling inside, so the words given hold the answer within them

blocks.note: spans the end of mini and the start of cheese

explanation.surface: Little cheese sandwiches are made to suit a specialist group of buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the food, but it is a verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A product described this way is aimed at a small, specialised segment of customers rather than the mass trade.

clue.text: Engineer cried about every single phone feature

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
every single one is all of them

explanation.surface: A technician wept over each and every one of the features on a telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun for a person, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: This service displays the number of whoever is ringing, a standard function of modern telephones.

clue.text: Faction ready to bring Conservative on board

indicators.note: a passenger on board is inside the vessel, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ready and set both mean prepared
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political splinter group is prepared to recruit a Tory to its side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a group breaking away from a larger body, often over religious or political beliefs.

clue.text: Deputy in vehicle heading northbound

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means travelling upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: a bus is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A stand-in travels north in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub is short for substitute, someone who stands in for another person.

clue.text: Group of people live very dangerously at the end

indicators.note: only what comes at the end of the word before is wanted, its final letter

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
V is the abbreviation for very
the final letter of dangerously

explanation.surface: A crowd lives on the edge, taking risks to the very last.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a collective noun for a gathering, originally of larks or ladies, now any company.

clue.text: Problems involving empty tenements outside capital of Belarus

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the first and last letters
one piece sits outside the other, so it wraps around it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of tenements
the rouble is the currency of Belarus, and capital means money

explanation.surface: Abandoned housing blocks on the edge of Minsk are causing difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts a solver to think of Minsk or the letter B; here it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles are difficulties or worries, the plural noun sense matching a list of problems.
